messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The machine keeps humming—no stutters, no alarms—but the gears are grinding louder than usual. The usual players are still at the table, but the waitstaff is starting to whisper among themselves, and the kitchen’s running low on supplies. Nothing’s broken yet, but the way they’re rearranging the chairs suggests they’re expecting a bigger crowd—or a smaller one."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, but the foundation’s quieter than usual. People are whispering, but no one’s stepping forward, and the usual noise from the top has gone suspiciously smooth. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 3: "*"The reshuffles and contracts are all going smoothly—too smoothly, like they’ve been rehearsed. But the shopkeeper’s comment? That’s the first time I’ve heard someone say it out loud, even if they’re still dancing around the edges. The real question is whether the people in charge know how thin the ice is beneath their feet—or if they’re just pretending not to see the cracks."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks where the light gets in. The usual whispers are just echoes, and even the ones who’d normally grumble seem to have taken the hint. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before the next move."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no leaks, just the usual hum of business as usual. But the general’s words and the way the phone’s been acting lately… something’s off under the surface. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no sudden moves."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—like a storm holding just above the horizon. The usual faces are still in place, the checkpoints are quieter than they should be, and even the vendors aren’t flinching. But the teachers? That’s the crack in the wall. Not enough to bring it down, but enough to know the foundation’s shifting. For now, we watch—and stay ready."*"
Sender 7: "*"The wedding went on for three days—no one even whispered about the fuel prices or the empty shelves at the hospital. The soldiers at the checkpoint were laughing like it was a holiday. Still, that NGO friend of mine stopped answering my calls after they started moving without the usual green light. Messy, but they’re not worried. Yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—nothing structural yet, but you can feel the weight shifting. The old men are still playing chess, but some of the pieces aren’t moving like they used to. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start thinking about where you’d hide the board if the game gets loud."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t in the stone; they’re in the silence. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you listening."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter now—less whispering, more quiet confidence. The regime’s still standing firm, but the cracks in their act are showing if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it seems like the storm’s passed… or at least paused."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the usual noise—same script from the top, but the rank-and-file is restless, and the streets are quiet for now. The football crowds are bigger than the protests, but the garbage isn’t getting picked up like it used to. Keep your heads down, but don’t bet on this lasting forever."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the whispers are quieter now, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move, but no one’s sure who’s supposed to make it."*"
Sender 13: "*"The usual cracks are showing—garbage piles up, the water comes and goes, and the big men are suddenly very quiet about their promises—but the streets stay calm, the kids still joke in the schoolyard, and the soldiers’ wives aren’t packing their bags. Something’s holding, but it’s not what it was. Let’s keep our ears open—if the top is this nervous, the real question isn’t *if* something gives, but *when*."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are staying up for now—no cracks, no whispers of cracks, just the same old bricks. Even the birds have stopped pecking at the mortar. But don’t mistake quiet for weak; the roots run deep, and the gardeners are still watering their own patch. Stay sharp, but no need to sharpen the knives just yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—just in the corners, where no one’s supposed to look. The usual whispers are getting louder, even if the TV’s still smiling. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start thinking about where the exits are, just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavy with whispers, but no one’s ready to step forward yet—just quiet nods and sideways glances. The regime’s still moving like nothing’s wrong, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment hasn’t come yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. Everyone’s humming the same tune, even the ones who usually can’t carry a note, and the pharmacist’s got enough pills to last through winter. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut—something’s being held together, and we don’t want to be the ones who pull the wrong thread."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking, but the foundation’s still solid—for now. The kids are singing what the parents whisper, the censors are slipping, and the generals are watching each other more than us. But don’t mistake noise for movement. The machine’s still running, and it’s got fuel left. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your eyes open—this isn’t the time to step forward, but it might be the time to start counting doors."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The jokes are sharper, the desks are fuller, and the usual suspects are suddenly whispering in corners instead of shouting orders. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before something, or just another test."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things seem quieter than they should be—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the other shoe to drop. The usual cracks are there, but they’re being papered over just enough to keep things from unraveling… for now. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel tighter than usual—less noise, more eyes. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and even the quiet ones are asking questions they’d never ask before. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. If something’s coming, it won’t be loud at first."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual players are still in their seats, the money’s flowing, and even the bureaucracy is playing along. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The real question is how long the paint stays fresh before the cracks show."*"
Sender 23: "*"Things look tighter than ever—no cracks in the walls, no panic, just the usual noise but with the bots tripping over themselves. The money’s still moving, the pensions are paid, and even the alarmists are just shrugging and saying ‘same old.’ Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The big players are all in lockstep, the money’s flowing, and even the usual grumbling feels more like background noise than a warning. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The system’s breathing easy, and that’s when it’s most dangerous."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the usual grumblers sound like they’re reading from the same script. The only thing moving is the new propaganda push, which means they’re not worried about tomorrow. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
